Implied against realised volatility on SPXW same-day options

    Feature
    Seller, for the charts and bucket tables

    1. Descriptive: the feature and the result over the same 30 minutes

    The feature uses the window's own realised volatility, which is known only when the window ends. This explains a result. It cannot be traded.

    2. Predictive: the feature known at the start, the result of the window that follows

    The trailing feature sets implied volatility at the window's start against the realised volatility of the 30 minutes just ended. The first window of each day has no window before it and is left out.

    3. Why the trailing feature does not predict

    Rank correlations inside each time of day, so the pattern of the day cannot produce them.

    How much of the next window's realised volatility each figure explains

    4. Time of day: what the market moved against what the options charged

    The plain ratio sets a window against implied volatility for the whole rest of the day. The window ratio sets it against what the options charged for that window alone. The line at 1 is "moved exactly what was charged".
